hypotheses.rationale: The used learning rate (3e-6) is far below the default 1e-5 and typical LoRA rates (~1e-4), which can cause the model to barely change from the base weights, resulting in poor accuracy despite decreasing loss.
A LoRA rank of 16 may be insufficient to capture the 77‑way classification mapping in a 0.6B model, limiting expressivity and causing the model to stall at low accuracy even after many epochs.

If training employed a chat template (e.g., with system/user/assistant tags) while inference expects a plain prompt‑label format, the model learns to predict tokens from the wrong context, yielding incorrect labels despite low loss.
Training examples are 45‑103 tokens, much shorter than the context length, and may not reflect the phrasing of the held‑out queries, leading to good validation loss but poor real‑world performance.
